title: Why LLMs Aren't Scientists Yet: Lessons from Four Autonomous Research Attempts

mechanism.domainTask: Case study of four LLM-driven autonomous machine-learning research attempts and their workflow failures
mechanism.populationDetail: The system routes research artifacts through workflow stages but does not maintain an evolutionary candidate population.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No elite solution archive is described; research papers and shared project files are not evolutionary archives.
mechanism.replacementDetail: A funnel shortlists research ideas and advances four selected attempts; this is workflow orchestration, not population replacement.
mechanism.generationDetail: Agents generate research ideas, hypotheses, plans, and outlines, but the paper does not define an evolutionary parent-offspring relation among candidate solutions.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Workflow-level checks assess hypothesis implementation fidelity, statistical validity, and readiness to write; feedback can route revisions, although most failed attempts were terminated by humans.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: No evolutionary parents are selected. The two papers combined for idea generation are literature inputs and must not be counted as true candidate parents.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: The central subject is orchestration and empirical failure analysis of autonomous scientific workflows, including human intervention and research-validity judgments, rather than evolutionary search mechanisms.
